title: A Special Person Day
strapline: For the grown-up who loves you — mums, dads, grandparents, whoever cares.
intent: Celebrating a special person honours the love in every child's life, in whatever shape their family takes.
Making a gift or card for someone they love grows care, effort and the joy of giving to another.
Talking about who cares for them builds each child's sense of family, belonging and identity.
Choosing every-family-included language — 'a special person' — makes sure no child feels left out.
The occasion sparks heartfelt creative work, from painting to card-making to little performances.
implementation: Keep it open and inclusive: children make something for a special grown-up who loves them — a parent, grandparent, carer, whoever it is.
Talk warmly about their special person: 'Who loves you and looks after you? What do you love doing together?'
Offer real creative choices — painting, card-making, a planted seed, a photo frame — so the gift is truly theirs.
Model the giving talk: 'How do you think they'll feel when you give them this? What shall we write inside?'
Be gently mindful of every family shape, and make sure each child has a special person to celebrate.
Follow the children — some will labour over one careful gift, others will make something for everyone they love.
key_questions: Who is a special person who loves and looks after you?
What do you love doing together?
What could you make that they would love?
How do you think they'll feel when you give it to them?
What would you like to say to them?

impact.text: Children talk about their family and the people who care for them.
Children make a gift or card with care, effort and their own choices.
Children show they notice and value how their special person feels.
Children take pride in giving something they made themselves.
Children use talk to express love and plan their gift.

enhancements: A card- and gift-making station with real creative choices.
A planted bulb or seed to grow and give.
A photo frame or handprint keepsake to decorate.
A 'my special person' talk-time or display.
A little performance or song to share with special people invited in.

playing_exploring: Children explore materials to make something special for someone they love.
They engage warmly with talk about their family and carers.
active_learning: Children put real care and effort into a gift and see it through.
They take pride in making and giving.
creating_thinking: Children plan a gift with their special person in mind.
They imagine how their gift will make someone feel.
